concept.shortdesc: The analytics user guide is intended for users interested in predictive maintenance analytics.

conbody.p: The analytics user guide is intended for users interested in predictive maintenance analytics.

concept.shortdesc: The ADI OtoSense™ Smart Motor Sensor (SMS) performs predictive maintenance on low-voltage 3-phase induction motors.

conbody.p: The ADI OtoSense™ Smart Motor Sensor (SMS) performs predictive maintenance on low-voltage 3-phase induction motors. It is a complete, easy-to-setup hardware and software solution that uses advanced sensors and AI-based data analysis to:

ul.li: provide round-the-clock condition-based monitoring of motor’s health. For example, power system, motor shaft balance, and overall performance issues.
provide fault notifications.
deliver electrical, mechanical, and thermal health diagnostics with severity levels
recommend solutions for identified motor and performance issues.

concept.shortdesc: This section describes the benefits provided by the SMS.

li.p: This section describes the benefits provided by the SMS.
The SMS translates the collected data into actionable insights. Here are some of the benefits of using the SMS:
Non-intrusive Installation: The SMS can be attached to active motors, ensuring continuous operation.

Enhanced Plant Efficiency: The SMS monitors the health of a motor’s components and sends alerts about anomalies and degradation that can lead to faults, enabling efficient maintenance planning and reducing unexpected breakdowns.
Secure Motor Data: The SMS safely stores the motor data on the ADI OtoSense™ Server.
Better Inventory Management: The SMS assists in identifying the required spare components, thereby assisting in minimizing surplus inventory and expenditure.
Reduced Maintenance Costs: The SMS helps extend motor life by providing maintenance insights that reduce repair costs and downtime.

concept.shortdesc: This section describes how the OtoSense ™ system works.

conbody.p: This section describes how the OtoSense ™ system works.
The hardware and software system consists of the following components:

ul.li: The SMS
Expert health monitoring software hosted on the ADI OtoSense™ Server
Mobile and web applications that allow customers to monitor the status of motors fitted with an SMS

conbody.p: After an SMS is configured and installed on a motor, it begins sending data to the ADI OtoSense™ server, which then begins a learning process where a unique, customized model is created for that particular motor. It measures the multi-axis vibration, magnetic field, ambient temperature, and temperature condition of the motor. With the help of this data, motor health degradation can be detected that could lead to motor faults in the power system, stator winding, rotor, motor shaft/balance, eccentricity, bearing, alignment, cooling system, attachment (i.e. loose foot), and overall motor performance.

topic.shortdesc: This section describes the operating modes of the OtoSense™ system, which include the learning mode,

body.p: This section describes the operating modes of the OtoSense™ system, which include the learning mode, the normal operation mode, and the motor condition mode.

concept.shortdesc: After the SMS is configured and installed on a motor, it begins sending data from

conbody.p: After the SMS is configured and installed on a motor, it begins sending data from its on-board sensors to the ADI OtoSense™ Server and initiates a learning process. During this learning process, the analytics create a unique, customized model of the motor whose data is received. At regular intervals, the SMS sends a 2.4 second sample of all sensor data to the ADI OtoSense™ Server.

title.ph: The SMS Communicating with the Cloud

conbody.p: After the learning mode, the ADI OtoSense™ Server uses the baseline model to detect motor performance anomalies and generate alerts about impending motor issues.

task.shortdesc: This section describes the OtoSense™ learning mode.

li.p: This section describes the OtoSense™ learning mode.
The ADI OtoSense™ SMS requires a learning period to capture the healthy operation of the motor.
The 2.4 second sample sent by the SMS to the Server includes:

ul.li: Vibration X-Axis (raw data)
Vibration Z-Axis (raw data)
Magnetic Field (raw data)
Environmental temperature
Motor temperature

context.p: The proprietary algorithm extracts the most useful parameters from the data samples to generate a baseline model tailored to each motor’s operation. This model will be used to monitor changes to the motor's health. placeholder

li.p: This learning mode has three stages:

ul.li: Quick Learning (approximately seven days)
Predictive Learning (approximately four weeks)
Fully Predictive (ongoing)

context.note: Note: During the entire learning mode, the motor should run at all RPMs, all temperatures and with all loads that will be seen by the motor in its normal envelope operation in order to create the best model.

concept.shortdesc: This section describes the quick learning stage of the learning mode.

conbody.p: This section describes the quick learning stage of the learning mode.
Aseven days are required an initial model of how the motor operates￼. Faults will not be predicted
During the Quick Learning stage, the status indicator on both the mobile and web application will remain blue with a Learning badge. For more information, see Figure 3. placeholder

title.ph: Mobile application screen showing the motors in learning mode

concept.shortdesc: This section describes the predictive learning stage of the learning mode.

conbody.p: This section describes the predictive learning stage of the learning mode.
After the Quick Learning stage, OtoSense ™ enters the Predictive Learning stage, which takes approximately four weeks ￼. This stage enables improved predictions for all detectable fault types.

During this stage, faults will be predicted within the parameters of the motor conditions that the SMS observed during Quick Learning. The motor model will continue to improve based on learnings from any changes to operational conditions.
During the Predictive Learning stage, the status indicator on both the mobile and web application will show the motor status. For more information, see Figure 3 and Figure 4.

concept.shortdesc: This section describes the fully predictive stage of the learning mode.

conbody.p: This section describes the fully predictive stage of the learning mode.
When Fully Predictive, the SMS is capable of detecting faults across all conditions observed throughout the Predictive Learning stage.

section.p: This section describes the normal operation mode of the SMS.

After the learning mode, the ADI OtoSense™ Cloud platform compares incoming sensor data to the baseline model to detect declining motor health. It identifies significant deviation from the baseline model to generate the health index on a scale of 1-10.

reference.shortdesc: This section describes the motor condition mode of the SMS.

li.p: This section describes the motor condition mode of the SMS.

After Normal Operation Mode is established, motor condition mode analyses the deviation from the baseline model to generate the status of the motor. Motor conditioning status is rated on a 1-10 scale.

row.entry: normal operation For example, see Figure 7.
monitoring is recommended For example, see Figure 8.
imminent motor failure For example, see Figure 9.

section.p: Based on incoming sensor data, ADI OtoSense™ Cloud analytics provides insight into nine motor attributes and overall motor performance as displayed in Table 2.

title.ph: Motor Attributes Monitored by the ADI OtoSense™ Cloud Platform

row.entry: Health of the three phases of the power supply. This could lead to a motor current imbalance.
Fault in one of the phases of the motor. This could cause an imbalance of the motor currents.
Fault related to short-circuit ring or rotor bar.
Fault related to unequal distribution of mass. This could cause the centre of gravity to shift from the centre of rotation.
Fault related to asymmetric air gap between the rotor and the stator.
Fault related to mechanical stress or contamination. This could cause small cracks or defects in the bearing and create vibration problems.
Fault that occurs when two rotating shafts (motor and load) are not aligned. This could cause external misalignment.
Fault with fans attached to the shaft or externally attached to the motor.
Fault with structural looseness. This occurs when the motor base (or connection to the motor base) is not properly tightened.
Motor not fixed to base frame

Overall increase in vibrations Unusual changes in motor RPM, motor load or temperatures. This indicates faults that do not correspond to any of the other nine fault categories, which could be related to machine process.

li.p: The ADI OtoSense™ SMS REST API include status and state properties which are fundamental for understanding motor condition mode:
status- indicates the overall connection status of the motor; online or disconnected, and last online datetime.

state- indicates the component with the most severe fault i.e. the lowest Fault Score Index (FSI) value. For example, if a motor has multiple components with faults, one an Alarm and another a Warning, the state property of the motor object's status will indicate alarm.
For more information on the component code and the motor log refer to Motor ObjectThis section describes the motor object..

reference.shortdesc: The ADI OtoSense™ SMS has three on-board sensors that collect the data used to monitor

section.p: The ADI OtoSense™ SMS has three on-board sensors that collect the data used to monitor any significant deviation from the established baseline model:

ul.li: Vibration sensors – sense vibration in the X- and Z- axes.
Magnetic field sensor - measures the magnetic field around a motor.
Temperature sensors – measure temperatures of the motor and the environment.

section.p: The REST API fetch data to display status updates on the web and mobile application. For more information, see Appendix B: Cloud Platform Parameters.

concept.shortdesc: This section describes the information and specifications related to vibration sensors on the SMS.

li.p: This section describes the information and specifications related to vibration sensors on the SMS.
Vibrations monitoring and analysis are at the core of most condition-based monitoring systems as vibrations and harmonic signatures are often the first indication of an impending motor failure.
ADI OtoSense™ SMS is equipped with a Vibration X-axis (tangential vibration) sensor and a Vibration Z-axis (axial vibration) sensor. For specifications, see Table 3.

conbody.p: Since each motor has a unique vibrational profile, the ADI OtoSense™ SMS first determines a motor’s baseline operating condition during the Learning Mode.

The REST API fetch the time and frequency domain data to display it on the web and mobile application. Signal processing allows for the quick identification of key signal characteristics which form the basis of the analysis.

topic.shortdesc: This section describes the motor object.

body.p: This section describes the motor object.

concept.shortdesc: The motor object consists of a components map. Each component has a Fault Score Index

conbody.p: The motor object consists of a components map. Each component has a Fault Score Index (FSI) and a Code. The FSI is a value between 0 and 10, which indicates the following motor conditions or state:

ul.li: FSI < ‘5ʼ: Alarm
FSI= ‘5ʼ or ‘6ʼ: Warning
FSI > ‘6ʼ: Good.

conbody.note: Note: The lower the FSI value the greater the severity of the component fault.
conbody.p: For each component in a Warning or an Alarm state, an appropriate Code is assigned by the ADI OtoSense™ Cloud analytics. Each code defines both the recommended Action and the Description of the associated fault.
Each component has multiple possible codes depending on the severity of the fault.

For example, a Power System component with an FSI of ‘3ʼ or ‘4ʼ will be assigned code ‘1002ʼ and a Power System component with an FSI of ‘2ʼ or below will be assigned code ‘1003ʼ. For more information, see Table 10.

Running flag 1 if running 0 if not running When the motor is rotating at a very low speed, less than 25% of its rated speed (rated RPM), the analytics may interpret the motor as stopped. running is used to calculate the Number of Starts in a time range. Chronologically sort the performance records in the time range and count the number of times _running_ transitions from '0' to '1'. This approximates the number of times the motor started in the specified time range.

reference.shortdesc: This section describes the parameters used to assess the condition of a motor component.

section.p: This section describes the parameters used to assess the condition of a motor component.

Each parameter in the following table represents the Fault Score Index (FSI) of the corresponding motor component condition. These predicted health indicators for motor components are generated each time the analytics processes data samples received from a running motor. The values are between zero and ten:

ul.li: A value of 10 corresponds to a perfect state for the component.
A value of 0 corresponds to a catastrophic state for the component.

row.entry: Problems in the three phases of the power supply, which could lead to a motor current imbalance.
Problems in one of the phases of the motor, which could cause an imbalance of the motor currents.
Short-circuit ring or rotor bar related problems.
Unequal distribution of mass, causing the center of gravity to shift from the center of rotation.
Asymmetric air gap between the rotor and stator.
Mechanical stress or contamination leading to small cracks or defects that occur in the bearing, creating vibration problems.
Occurs when two rotating shafts (motor and load) are not aligned, creating external misalignment.
Problems with fans attached to the shaft or externally attached to the motor.
Structural looseness occurring when the motor base (or connection to the motor base) is not properly tightened.

Used to capture abnormal events such as an overall increase in vibrations, unusual changes in motor RPM, motor load or temperatures, etc. Indicates faults that do not correspond to any of the other nine fault categories, which could be related to machine process.
